title: China champions open AI to the world. In private, it’s afraid of one closed American model.
excerpt: China champions open AI to the world but privately fears one closed American model it cannot access: Anthropic's Mythos, weeks before Xi meets Trump.
content_html:
China has spent the past year telling the world that AI should be open, cheap and shared. In private, its officials are unnerved by one American model that is none of those things.

Beijing is growing anxious that Anthropic’s Mythos could be turned against it, Bloomberg reported. Officials see the frontier model as a potential offensive cyber weapon, people familiar with the matter said, and they resent that Anthropic denies China access even for ordinary use.

The fear is not abstract. Mythos has proved unusually good at breaking software, finding and exploiting flaws at a scale humans cannot match. One GovTech assessment found it chained hundreds of vulnerabilities together and wrote working exploit code on its first attempt. That worked more than 83% of the time. In June, Washington judged the risk severe enough to cut off foreign access entirely.

The irony is hard to miss. China is the loudest champion of open AI, flooding the world with downloadable models and casting itself as the technology’s democratiser. Yet the system it fears most is a closed American one it cannot legally touch.

A grievance with a summit attached

The timing sharpens everything. Xi Jinping is due in the US on 24 September, and Beijing wants a warm mood beforehand. Officials are seeking a “win-win” tone at AI talks expected ahead of the meeting. Suspicion, though, runs both ways. Washington worries that Chinese firms are quietly training their own models on American ones.

That worry has teeth. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent floated sanctions last month against developers found to have stolen intellectual property, after Beijing’s Moonshot AI released a system said to rival the best US labs. China’s Commerce Ministry warned it would take “all necessary measures” in reply.

Anthropic sits at the centre of the distrust, by choice. It has become the most China-hawkish of the US labs. Chief executive Dario Amodei wants high-end chips kept out of the country, has accused Alibaba’s Qwen team of training on Claude’s outputs, and has called China’s ruling party “the most capable threat” among authoritarian governments. Beijing’s suspicion, in other words, is not imagined.

The response Beijing is drawing up

China is not acting yet, but it is preparing. Officials are drafting options should Washington move first, the people said, including sanctions or adding US AI firms to a restricted-entity list. Because Anthropic does not operate in China, any such penalty would carry little commercial sting. It would be a signal, not a blow.

Beijing has shown it will send those signals. In June it placed export controls on two American rare-earth firms after the Pentagon added Alibaba and BYD to a military-linked blacklist, part of a pattern of hitting back where it hurts. AI is simply the newest front in a rivalry that already spans chips, robots and rare earths.

Washington is caught in its own contradiction. Trump says he is weighing tighter AI controls while fearing they could hobble American firms. “We have to be careful in both ways,” he said last week. “We don’t want to restrict them where all of a sudden, we come in second to China.”

His own government has meanwhile banned federal agencies from using Anthropic’s tools, a fight the company is contesting in court.

So the two superpowers now treat frontier models the way they once treated missiles. The model China fears most is one it cannot download, built by the company most determined to keep it that way. That standoff is the new front, and it opens just as the two leaders sit down to talk.

content_html_zh:
过去一年，中国一直告诉世界人工智能应该开放、廉价和共享。 私下里，官员们对一种与上述情况无关的美国模式感到不安。

据彭博社报道，北京越来越担心人类的神话可能会被用来反对它。 知情人士表示，官员们将前沿模型视为潜在的进攻性网络武器，他们对 Anthropic 拒绝中国访问（即使是普通用途）也感到不满。

这种恐惧并不是抽象的。 事实证明，Mythos 在破坏软件、发现和利用缺陷方面表现得异常出色，其规模是人类无法比拟的。 一项 GovTech 评估发现，它将数百个漏洞链接在一起，并在第一次尝试时编写了有效的漏洞利用代码。 这在超过 83% 的时间里都有效。 六月，华盛顿判断风险严重到足以完全切断外国准入。

其中的讽刺意味不容忽视。 中国是开放人工智能最响亮的拥护者，向世界提供了大量可下载的模型，并将自己塑造为该技术的民主化者。 然而，它最担心的是一个它无法合法触及的封闭的美国体系。

附带峰会的不满

时机让一切变得更加尖锐。 习近平将于 9 月 24 日访问美国，北京方面希望事先有一个温暖的气氛。 官员们希望在会议之前的人工智能会谈中寻求“双赢”的基调。 然而，怀疑是双向的。 华盛顿担心中国公司正在悄悄地模仿美国的模式来训练自己的模式。

这种担忧是有牙齿的。 在北京的 Moonshot AI 发布了据称可与美国最好的实验室相媲美的系统后，财政部长斯科特·贝森特 (Scott Bessent) 上个月对被发现窃取知识产权的开发商实施了制裁。 中国商务部警告称，将采取“一切必要措施”予以回应。

人择自然而然地成为了不信任的中心。 它已成为美国对华最为鹰派的实验室。 首席执行官达里奥·阿莫代(Dario Amodei)希望高端芯片不要进入中国，指责阿里巴巴的Qwen团队利用克劳德的产品进行训练，并称中国执政党是独裁政府中“最有能力的威胁”。 换句话说，北京的怀疑不是想象的。

北京正在制定回应

中国还没有行动，但已经在做准备了。 知情人士称，如果华盛顿首先采取行动，官员们正在起草选择方案，包括制裁或将美国人工智能公司列入限制实体名单。 由于 Anthropic 不在中国开展业务，任何此类处罚都不会带来什么商业刺激。 这将是一个信号，而不是打击。

北京已表明将发出这些信号。 今年六月，五角大楼将阿里巴巴和比亚迪列入与军方有关的黑名单后，美国对两家美国稀土公司实施了出口管制，这是一种回击模式的一部分。 人工智能只是芯片、机器人和稀土领域竞争的最新前沿。

华盛顿陷入了自己的矛盾之中。 特朗普表示，他正在考虑加强对人工智能的控制，同时担心这可能会阻碍美国公司。 “我们必须在这两方面都要小心，”他上周表示。 “我们不想限制他们，让我们突然成为仅次于中国的国家。”

与此同时，他自己的政府已禁止联邦机构使用 Anthropic 的工具，该公司正在法庭上对此进行抗辩。

因此，这两个超级大国现在对待前沿模型就像对待导弹一样。 中国最担心的模式是它无法下载的模式，而这种模式是由最决心保持这种状态的公司打造的。 这场对峙是新的战线，就在两位领导人坐下来交谈时它就打开了。
